clue.text: Foolhardy rascal can show concern

blocks.note: a little devil is a mischievous rascal
may and can both express permission or possibility
to care is to show concern

explanation.surface: A reckless scoundrel turns out to have a caring side after all.
explanation.definitionFit: A devil-may-care attitude is reckless and careless of consequences, which is what foolhardy describes.

clue.text: Nearest resort in the orient

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for an adjective meaning located in or belonging to the east

indicators.note: read as re-sort, sorting the letters again into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be re-sorted

explanation.surface: A traveller looks for the closest holiday resort somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday destination, but split as re-sort it tells you to rearrange the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is the East, so anything found in or typical of that part of the world is Eastern.

clue.text: Ladies to move far from the others

indicators.note: letters that move change their places, giving a new arrangement

blocks.note: the eight letters to be moved around

explanation.surface: Some women are asked to go and sit well apart from the rest of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Something isolated is set apart, remote and cut off, lying a long way from everything else.

clue.text: Child power makes itself heard

indicators.note: something that makes itself heard is spoken, so we want the sound of the word rather than its spelling

blocks.note: might is strength or power

explanation.surface: A small child with a loud voice shows its strength by being noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: A mite is an affectionate word for a small child, as in 'poor little mite'.

clue.text: Cowardly character shown up by the referee?

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the thing a referee holds up, standing for the noun

blocks.note: yellow is slang for cowardly
a card is an eccentric or amusing character

explanation.surface: A coward's true nature is exposed by an official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shown up' suggests exposed as a fraud; here it means literally held up in the air, as a football referee does to caution a player.
explanation.definitionFit: In football the referee holds up a yellow card to book a player for an offence, a formal warning.

clue.text: It's a crime, so ran when disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed letters are knocked out of their order and rearranged

blocks.note: the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A burglar commits an offence and flees when interrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Language you must understand

blocks.note: surface reading: some tongue that everyone is required to know
setter's reading: you have to know this tongue just to read the clue itself

explanation.surface: A teacher insists there is one tongue every pupil has to learn.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: it is written in a language, and that is the one the solver must understand to be reading it.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue is printed in the language of England, which any reader of the puzzle must know.

clue.text: Advice note can change ' prior announcement (7.8) ' -

indicators.note: to change the letters is to alter their order into something new

blocks.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A recommendation in writing could alter an earlier public statement.
explanation.definitionFit: Advance notice is a warning given beforehand, an announcement made prior to the event.

clue.text: Aren't they particular what they sell?

definitions.text: Aren't they particular what they sell?

blocks.note: surface reading: are these shopkeepers fussy about their goods?
setter's reading: particular is the opposite of general, so these shops sell everything rather than particular lines

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders whether certain shops are fussy about their stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Particular' seems to mean choosy; it is really the opposite of general, describing a shop with no special line.
explanation.definitionFit: General stores sell a wide range of everyday goods instead of specialising in one kind of merchandise.

clue.text: Get into bad shape

blocks.note: surface reading: become unfit through lack of exercise
setter's reading: to put something into a twisted, misshapen form

explanation.surface: Someone lets their fitness slip and grows flabby.
explanation.definitionFit: To distort something is to twist or bend it out of its proper form, giving it a warped outline.

clue.text: Angela's cooked an Italian dish

indicators.note: cooked figuratively means tampered with, so the letters are altered in order

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman called Angela has made a pasta dish for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is a baked Italian pasta dish layered with meat sauce and cheese.

clue.text: Kipling's wolf emerging from a lake

indicators.note: something emerging from these letters is a new form produced out of them

blocks.note: the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wolf from a Kipling story climbs out of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Akela is the lead wolf of the pack in Kipling's The Jungle Book, also the title of a Cub Scout leader.

clue.text: Match money playing dice

indicators.note: dice that are playing are rolled and tumble about, so their letters are shuffled

blocks.note: a coin is a piece of money
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gambler bets cash on a game of dice to settle a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a game to be won with money; it is a verb meaning agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that coincide correspond exactly or happen at the same time, so they match.

clue.text: Striking reminder of a Lowry figure

definitions.text: Striking reminder of a Lowry figure

blocks.note: surface reading: a memorable or vivid evocation of a painting
setter's reading: something struck to light a fire, which also names the thin stick people in L. S. Lowry's paintings

explanation.surface: Something vividly calls to mind a figure painted by L. S. Lowry.
explanation.walkthrough: L. S. Lowry was an English painter of crowded northern street scenes, famous for thin figures nicknamed matchstick men.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchstick is struck to make a flame, and Lowry's spindly people are popularly called matchstick men.

clue.text: Document required when handing over a vehicle

blocks.note: first meaning: the legal deed transferring ownership of property
second meaning: a means of transport

explanation.surface: Paperwork is needed when a car is passed on to a new owner.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs the two meanings together as a car sale; they are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A conveyance is both the legal deed that transfers property and, more formally, any means of transport such as a carriage.

clue.text: He put in a word of thanks for the goddess

indicators.note: one item put in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: ta is an informal British way of saying thank you
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man says a quick thank-you to a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, British slang for thanks, opens to hold HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thea, or Theia, is a Titan goddess in Greek mythology, mother of the sun and moon.

clue.text: A sharp fall in sweet production?

definitions.text: A sharp fall in sweet production?

blocks.clueFragment: A sharp fall in sweet production
blocks.note: surface reading: a steep decline in the output of a confectionery factory
setter's reading: a sour-tasting drop, which is a kind of boiled sweet

explanation.surface: A confectionery business suffers a steep slump in output.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'sharp' as sour and 'fall' as a drop; together they name a sweet, which is the product made. An acid drop is a sour boiled sweet popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid drop is a tangy boiled sweet, literally a sour drop of candy, the product of a sweet maker.

clue.text: Insensitive one, for example, displays no hesitation

indicators.note: showing none of something means that part is left out

blocks.note: one is an example of a number
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: An unfeeling person shows no hesitation at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Take NUMBER and drop the hesitant ER from its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Numb means without sensation or feeling, so it describes someone or something insensitive.

clue.text: Strikes that don't come off?

blocks.note: surface reading: industrial walkouts that never actually happen
setter's reading: blows at a ball that fail to connect properly

explanation.surface: Planned industrial action by workers comes to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikes' suggests trade-union walkouts; here they are swings at a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishit is a badly struck shot in a ball game, a stroke that does not succeed as intended.

clue.text: They don't have to be smart to fool the birds

definitions.text: They don't have to be smart to fool the birds

blocks.clueFragment: They don't have to be smart
blocks.note: surface reading: you need no cleverness to trick birds
setter's reading: smart as in well dressed, since these figures stand in fields wearing old rags

explanation.surface: It takes no great intelligence to trick a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' seems to mean clever; it means neatly dressed, and the figures in question wear tattered clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarecrows are ragged human figures set up in fields so that birds take fright and keep off the crops.

clue.text: Hackneyed tour now reorganised

indicators.note: reorganising puts the letters into a different arrangement

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tired old sightseeing trip has been given a new itinerary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outworn is stale and overused, like a cliché that has lost its freshness through repetition.

clue.text: Matchbox model

blocks.note: a Test is an international match, especially in cricket
a case is a box or container

explanation.surface: A tiny toy car from the Matchbox range.
explanation.walkthrough: Matchbox, a brand of toy model cars, has to be split into its two halves; 'model' is then the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a legal action whose outcome serves as a model or precedent for similar cases.

clue.text: Is unable to write love song

blocks.note: can't means is unable, apostrophe dropped
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A songwriter suffers writer's block and cannot compose a love song.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is a section of a long poem, originally one meant to be sung, so it is a form of song.

clue.text: Said by the Frenchman to be the same

blocks.note: dit is French for said
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Frenchman claims two things are identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is used to show that something repeats what came before, meaning the same again.

clue.text: Bespectacled greeting in American state

indicators.note: someone bespectacled has a pair of round lenses around the eyes, so the word is framed on either side

blocks.note: a pair of spectacles looks like two round O shapes side by side
hi is a casual greeting

explanation.surface: Someone wearing glasses says hello somewhere in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The two round lenses of a pair of glasses are pictured as two O shapes, one on each side of HI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohio is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Put a chit in for wine

indicators.note: put here means placed afresh, so the letters are set down in a new order

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A customer hands in a voucher to claim a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: A chit is a short note or voucher, often used to claim something.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from the Tuscany region of Italy.

clue.text: Abhor money though some is essential for growth

indicators.note: some means only part of the words that come before is used

blocks.note: found running across the end of the first word and most of the second

explanation.surface: You may hate money, but a certain amount is needed for a business to expand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abhor money though some' reads as a moral about wealth; 'some' marks part of the first two words as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hormones such as growth hormone are chemical messengers the body needs in order to develop and grow.

clue.text: US rep dealing in shares?

blocks.note: first meaning: an American repertory theatre troupe performing a stock of plays
second meaning, whimsically: a firm whose business is stocks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rep' looks like a sales representative; it is short for repertory theatre. The question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a stock company is a resident theatre troupe, and the phrase also describes a joint-stock business with shareholders.
